{{Quote|Ah, there she is&mdash;the ''Ebon Hawk''. My pride and joy; the fastest ship in the Outer Rim!|Davik Kang gloats about his modified ''Dynamic''-class freighter|<ref name="KOTOR1" />}}
The '''''Dynamic''-class freighter''' was a [[Light freighter/Legends|light freighter]] built by a [[Unidentified Core Galaxy Systems subsidiary|subsidiary]] of [[Core Galaxy Systems]] on the remote [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Transel]] around the period of the [[Mandalorian Wars]]. A stock ''Dynamic''-class [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] was only modestly armed and shielded; however, the ship was designed to accept modifications without compromising existing systems and most ships were therefore heavily customized by their owners. Though prized for its ability to be modified with ease&mdash;a trait advertised by the class's name&mdash;''Dynamic''-class [[Starship/Legends|starships]] were rare throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] as only one ship was produced at a time. ''Dynamic''-class freighters had relatively less area onboard to hold cargo than other light freighters but possessed ample space for passengers, allowing the class to operate as a [[Transport/Legends|transport]]. Some of the class's distinct elements such as the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] and saucer-shaped [[Hull/Legends|hull]] designs, would appear in later craft; [[starshipwright]] [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] drew inspiration from the freighter when designing some of their own ships, including the [[YT-series/Legends|YT-series]] freighters released several millennia after the ''Dynamic''-class starship began production.

One of the most notable ''Dynamic''-class freighters, the ''[[Ebon Hawk]]'', played a key role in both the [[Jedi Civil War]] and later [[Dark Wars]]. The ship, so heavily modified that it was difficult to ascertain the ship's builder or origins, was originally owned by various members of the [[Exchange]] and [[Taris/Legends|Tarisian]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Davik Kang]] before [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], an amnesic Republic [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] and unknowingly the former [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], stole the ship to escape the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Fleet/Legends|fleet's]] [[Destruction of Taris|bombardment of Taris]] during the Jedi Civil War. Shortly thereafter, Revan&mdash;as a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] and aware of his former position&mdash;used the ''Ebon Hawk'' in [[Gender/Legends|his]] quest to locate the Sith [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] known as the [[Star Forge]], and later on a journey through the galaxy's [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] before his capture. The ''Ebon Hawk'' would eventually resurface under the command of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] exile [[Meetra Surik]], who used it on her quest to locate several [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] in hiding after the [[First Jedi Purge]] and, later, the elimination of the [[Sith Triumvirate]]. Surik would take the ship back into the Unknown Regions to locate the captured Revan, but her [[Death/Legends|death]] and Revan's continued imprisonment left the ''Ebon Hawk'' stranded with no owner.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|It's got a temperamental hyperdrive, and the turrets can be sluggish and unresponsive against fast moving fighters.|[[Ratrin Vhek]], speaking of a heavily modified ''Dynamic''-class freighter|<ref name="KOTOR2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>}}
Designed and produced one at a time on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Transel]], the ''Dynamic''-class [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] cost 80,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] for a new [[Starship/Legends|starship]], while used ships sold for 30,000 credits. The [[Light freighter/Legends|light freighter]] was designed and built with modification in mind; as a stock ''Dynamic''-class ship possessed only modest weaponry and shielding, most buyers often took advantage of this adaptive engineering to customize their freighters with more powerful systems. Though not recognized for their speed or toughness, ''Dynamic''-class freighters were regarded as sturdy builds; coupled with the ease of modification, the ship was prized amongst [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] and [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] alike. A [[Hyperdrive/Legends|class 3 hyperdrive]] and [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computer]] allowed the vessel to move through [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] to destinations throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Landing gear allowed the freighter to berth planetside and aboard larger vessels and [[Space station/Legends|space stations]].<ref name="SOTG07" />
[[File:Dynamic-class.png|thumb|left|230px|Deck plans for a stock ''Dynamic''-class freighter]]
The ship could be crewed by two [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] and supported six passengers, allowing it to comfortably function as a [[Transport/Legends|transport]]. An onboard [[Medical bay/Legends|medical bay]], located near the central main hold, could provide limited triage options for injured beings. In case of emergency, such as a [[Hull/Legends|hull]] breach, every room aboard the ship was equipped with [[Airlock/Legends|airlocks]] which could seal shut, containing the compromised sections and retaining the atmosphere in unaffected areas. The ship carried two [[Standard month/Legends|standard months]] worth of consumables, allowing the crew to make extended trips.<ref name="SOTG07" />

Three prongs formed a trident-shaped hull fore of the freighter's midpoint, with the central protrusion extending the farthest. The prongs were asymmetrical; a hull section, containing a landing ramp, was located between the central and starboard prongs. The boxy central section of the ship, with a [[Viewport/Legends|viewport]] located at its fore, held the ship's [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] and [[Comlink/Legends|communications]] station. These two rooms were connected via a long hallway to the ship's main hold, located at the ship's center. The flanking port and starboard prongs were mirrored images of each other and contained crew bunks and amenities. A lateral break in the ship's hull plating marked the freighter's midpoint. For armament, a pair of large [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]] were mounted port and starboard, and dorsal and ventral [[Turret/Legends|turrets]] could be installed just behind the central prong. A ladder, located just behind the main hold, allowed access to these turrets.<ref name="SOTG07" />

The freighter's hull aft of midpoint formed a half-saucer with the fore of the ship. This distinctive design allowed the ship to fit the same area for cargo and systems as a larger, more angular hull; other shipbuilders would later mimic this design even millennia later. Two cargo areas, flanking the [[Engine/Legends|engine]] room in the central aft of the ship, could store 60 [[Metric ton/Legends|tons]] of cargo. The starboard cargo area was large enough to function as a garage,<ref name="SOTG07" /> with ample space to store a [[Swoop/Legends|swoop bike]] and workstation,<ref name="KOTOR1" /> and connected directly to the landing ramp. Two large, circular engines were mounted to the very back of the ship and provided the thrust necessary for the ship to move through [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]] at 800 [[Kilometer per hour/Legends|km/h]]. ''Dynamic''-class freighters often had a predominately [[Color/Legends|grey]] hull with reddish-orange accents adorning the ship's fore prongs, engine cowlings, and a radial band on the aft saucer section of the hull.<ref name="SOTG07" />

==History==
[[Starshipwright]] [[Core Galaxy Systems]] purchased an [[Unidentified Core Galaxy Systems subsidiary|independent company]] with a single manufacturing plant on the remote Republic<ref name="SOTG07" /> [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] world of Transel in the [[Transel system/Legends|Transel system]]<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> in a wave of expansion. Following a corporate reorganization, the Transel-based subsidiary was granted ongoing funding but a lack of oversight which allowed the continued production of a single ''Dynamic''-class freighter at a time. The company relied on the tendency for starship owners to modify their vessels when they designing the ''Dynamic''-class freighter and built their ship to easily adapt to any customization. Even the line's name was chosen to reflect this philosophy. As a result, most freighters in operation were heavily modified.<ref name="SOTG07" />

The class was utilized in a number of scenarios during [[Mandalorian Wars]], the galaxy-spanning series of conflicts between [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] warriors and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> A ''Dynamic''-class starship was part of the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic fleet]] over the [[Ralltiir system/Legends|Ralltiir system]] in 3963 BBY;<ref name="SW:KOTOR13:DoFP1" /> the freighter also appeared above [[Taris/Legends|Taris]] during the [[Taris Siege|Mandalorian invasion of Taris]].<ref name="SW:KOTOR23:KoSP2">[[Knights of the Old Republic 23|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 23]]</ref> Shortly after, around [[3951 BBY]], a [[Nashuaga|crash-landed ''Dynamic''-class freighter]] located within the [[Wavelength Gale's hidden cove|hidden base]] of smuggling group [[Wavelength Gale]] on the planet [[Volik]] was the rumored resting spot of the [[Mask of Darth Nihilus|mask]] of [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Nihilus]].<ref name="WizNihilus">{{WizCite|book=The Unknown Regions|story=The Mask of Darth Nihilus}}</ref>

===The ''Ebon Hawk''===
[[File:Leviathan_Ebon_Hawk.png|thumb|left|230px|The ''Ebon Hawk'', a modified ''Dynamic''-class freighter, evades blaster fire]]
Perhaps the most notorious starship of the class was the heavily modified ''[[Ebon Hawk]]'', owned by a number of notorious criminal groups, including the [[Exchange]], and engineered to perform well beyond its stock specifications.<ref name="SWDB" /> The ''Ebon Hawk'' played a pivotal role during the [[Jedi Civil War]] fought between Republic and [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] forces in [[3956 BBY]]<ref name="NEC" /> when [[Revan/Legends|Revan]],<ref name="KOTOR1" /> an amnesiac Republic [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]]<ref name="TOREncyc">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> who was also unknowningly the former [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] and commander of the Sith, stole the heavily-modified freighter from Tarisian [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Davik Kang]] and used it to escape the [[Destruction of Taris|bombardment of Taris]] by the Sith [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] at the command of Revan's former student, [[Darth Malak]]. Revan continued to use the ship in [[Gender/Legends|his]] campaign to locate the [[Star Forge]], an ancient [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] and factory used by the Sith. After the station's destruction and [[Death/Legends|death]] of Malak,<ref name="KOTOR1" /> Revan continued to use the ship while exploring the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] until his capture, at which point his [[Cleaning droid/Legends|utility droid]] [[T3-M4]] took command.<ref name="TOR:Revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref>

The ''Ebon Hawk'' later returned to known space<ref name="KOTOR2" /> in 3951 BBY during the [[Dark Wars]],<ref name="NEC" /> which saw the destruction of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and the resurgence of Sith forces, where the ship came under attack and was critically disabled. Once repaired, the ''Ebon Hawk'' again played a role against the Sith after [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] exile [[Meetra Surik]] acquired and used the freighter while locating a number of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] in hiding after the [[First Jedi Purge]]. During Surik's travels, [[Onderon/Legends|Onderonian]] [[General/Legends|general]] [[Vaklu]] falsely portrayed the ''Ebon Hawk''&mdash;which had been involved in a [[Starfighter combat/Legends|small-scale conflict]] with Onderanian forces&mdash;to be a [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] in order to spark [[Onderon Civil War|civil war]] on his home planet. Surik's efforts eventually culminated with the elimination of the [[Sith Triumvirate]] and the [[Battle of Malachor|destruction]] of fractured planet [[Malachor V]], though her ''Dynamic''-class freighter was heavily damaged during landing. Still, the ship managed to escape the planet's destruction<ref name="KOTOR2" /> and Surik used the ship to return to the Unknown Regions in an effort to find Revan, though she lost her own life in her search. Her death, Revan's continued imprisonment, and T3-M4's destruction left the ''Ebon Hawk'' stranded with no owner.<ref name="TOR:Revan" />

===Legacy===
Certain design elements of the ''Dynamic''-class freighter persisted throughout galactic history. Sometime during the [[Great Galactic War]] fought between the Galactic Republic and [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], shipbuilder [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] borrowed certain ''Dynamic''-class traits, including the half-saucer and cockpit, to produce the [[XS stock light freighter/Legends|XS stock light freighter]].<ref name="MFOWM">''[[Millennium Falcon Owner's Workshop Manual]]''</ref> CEC even compared the ''Dynamic''-class freighter to their new ship, showcasing their advancements in freighter design.<ref name="TORHolonet">{{Holonet|starships|xs-freighter|XS Freighter}}</ref> Millennia later, Corellian Engineering Corporation again drew on features from the ''Dynamic''-class freighter via their own ancient XS stock ships when designing a new line of freighters. The inspiration provided by the ancient ships eventually led to the creation of the [[YT-series/Legends|YT-series]], CEC's most popular line of freighters bearing some of their most recognizable starships, including the [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]].<ref name="MFOWM" />

==Behind the scenes==
The ''Dynamic''-class freighter first appeared in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'',<ref name="KOTOR1" /> released in [[2003]],<ref name="Anniversary">{{SW|url=news/kotor-galaxy-of-heroes|text=BioWare and Capital Games on Bringing ''KotOR'' Fan Favorites into ''Galaxy of Heroes''|nolive=1}}</ref> as the ''Ebon Hawk''.<ref name="KOTOR1" /> Supplemental material to the game, including the ship's [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry on [[StarWars.com]], hinted that the origins of the ship were a mystery thanks to its extensive modification.<ref name="SWDB" /> The class would appear in various other material, including the [[2004]]<ref name="Gamespot">{{GameSpot|url=star-wars-knights-of-the-old-republic-ii-the-sit|text=Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II - Rise of the Sith Lords}}</ref> video game [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords|sequel]] to ''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic'',<ref name="KOTOR2" /> but wouldn't receive a name until the [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]] sourcebook [[Starships of the Galaxy (Saga Edition)|''Starships of the Galaxy'']]<ref name="SOTG07" /> published in [[2007]].<ref name="SOTGrelease">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/starshipsgalaxy|text=''Starships of the Galaxy''}}</ref>

In the ''Dynamic''-class freighter's most featured role as the ''Ebon Hawk'' in the ''Knights of the Old Republic'' series, the ship was used in-game as a "hub", allowing players to travel from world to world and use onboard systems to upgrade equipment. [[BioWare]], the game's designers, intended to evoke the feeling of the ''[[Millennium Falcon/Legends|Millennium Falcon]]'',<ref name="SWDB" /> [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo's]] YT-1300 freighter prominently featured in the [[original trilogy]] of the [[Star Wars (Hasbro toy line)|Star Wars Saga]],<ref name="NEC" /> in both role and functionality. As a result, the ''Dynamic''-class freighter shares several similarities to the YT-1300 light freighter, including the turrets, raised tubular hull sections, and dish-like shape. As many of the systems of the ''Ebon Hawk'' were so heavily modified that it was hard determine even its manufacturer or place of origin, some, if not all, of the individual ship's specifications and abilities may have differed from the stock class,<ref name="SWDB" /> though the figures and features shown in ''Starships of the Galaxy'', including deckplans, are specifically designated as belonging to a stock ''Dynamic''-class freighter.<ref name="SOTG07" />
